thought.text: The docker healthcheck itself shows spring-app as **(healthy)** — that's definitive (Docker probes 8081/health). My manual `/dev/tcp` probe is just unreliable. Let me confirm cleanly and check the leftover serve process:

reasoning_content:
The backend health probe is returning only "0" (chunk length) — this time the body is missing. The previous successful probe returned the JSON body. Let me look more carefully — the "0" is the final chunked encoding terminator. It's possible the response body is being truncated. Let me test with a different approach and check whether the backend is actually healthy.

The container shows as "healthy" in docker ps (urbo-workspace-spring-app-1 Up 4 hours (healthy)). This is Docker's own health check that accesses 127.0.0.1:8081 /health. So the backend is definitely UP.

The reason my manual /dev/tcp probe is flaky is because the response isn't being fully captured. Let me verify with a cleaner method.

Actually, wait — docker ps shows spring-app as "(healthy)" — that's the definitive confirmation. Let me confirm it cleanly once more and move on.

Let me restart the app and cms dev servers. The boards server (39003) is still running. There are 2 serve.mjs processes (154203 = the boards serve, 161930 = probably a leftover). Let me check what 161930 is — it might be an app or cms serve that's still "alive" but whose build died.

First let me fix the backend health check, then bring up app and cms one at a time.

action.command:
echo "=== docker health (authoritative) ==="; docker inspect -f '{{.State.Health.Status}} (started {{.State.Health.StartedAt}})' urbo-workspace-spring-app-1
echo "=== spring-app logs: started/ready ==="; docker logs urbo-workspace-spring-app-1 2>&1 | grep -iE "Started UrboCmsApplication|Netty started|Tomcat started|Started .*Application" | tail -3
echo "=== what is serve proc 161930? ==="; cat /proc/161930/cmdline 2>/dev/null | tr '\0' ' '; echo
echo "=== check each serve's app via its logs ==="; for f in app cms boards; do echo "--$f (last line)--"; tail -1 /workspace/.urbo/workspace/logs/$f.log; done
